eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 3, Lesson 11
subtitle: pandas begins — the table you already know from SQL.

code:
import pandas as pd

prices = pd.Series([19.99, 45.0, 12.5],
                    index=["A1", "B2", "C3"],
                    name="price")
print(prices)
# A1 19.99 / B2 45.00 / C3 12.50
caption: A Series is a NumPy array that carries an index and an optional name.
Pull a value out by label; math applies to every value at once, like NumPy's vectorization.

eyebrow: The DataFrame: a table in memory
caption: Compare to SELECT * FROM customers — same columns; the row labels on the left are pandas' index.

code:
type(customers["city"])
# pandas.core.series.Series

customers["city"]

caption: A DataFrame is a dictionary-like collection of Series sharing an index.

code:
customers.shape      # (5, 4)   rows, columns
customers.columns    # Index(['customer_id', 'name', 'city', 'segment'])
customers.index      # RangeIndex(start=0, stop=5, step=1)
customers.dtypes     # customer_id int64; others object
caption: Attributes, not methods — no parentheses. Text columns show up as object in pandas 1.x.
